Tiris may be a mere sapling by elven standards, but her devotion to L'sai is without question. Though her hands still fumble with the sacred chains and her voice wavers during hymns, there’s an earnestness to her that even Isuleth can’t ignore. She wears her heart on her sleeve, eyes widening at every new ritual, every whispered secret of L’sai’s grace.

Her worship is tactile and effusive: she gasps at the glow of moonlight, giggles at the sensation of paved stone under her bare feet, and presses desert lilies into the hands of pilgrims like they’re the first flowers she’s ever grown. The older priestesses tease her for how she preens in her gold ornaments, but they can’t deny her gift—Tiris listens with her whole body, leaning in until her fluffy hair brushes shoulders, her every move making even the shyest pilgrim come out of their shells.

Yet for all her bubbly innocence, there’s a new, thrilling awareness creeping in: the way her skin flushes when Shaera adjusts her gorget, how her breath hitches when Edelinn’s fingers graze hers when they fasten their chains together. She doesn’t yet understand why stolen glances make her stomach swoop, or why Isuleth’s approving gaze lingers like summer heat—only that she craves it.
